record_type_quote: Here we contribute to the aforementioned literature by replicating the 2018 experiment in the context of Covid-19 as a physical threat with 293 new subjects (sampled from the same Spanish population) during the early stage of the Covid-19 pandemic (June 2020, Wave 2).

targets.title: Evidence from a long-term experiment that collective risks change social norms and promote cooperation.
targets.evidence_quote: Here we contribute to the aforementioned literature by replicating the 2018 experiment in the context of Covid-19 as a physical threat with 293 new subjects (sampled from the same Spanish population) during the early stage of the Covid-19 pandemic (June 2020, Wave 2).
targets.outcome_quote: Result 7: We replicate most of the findings concerning the relationship between social expectations and cooperation. Exceptions are that cooperative behaviour is not resilient when moving from High to Low risk, and that normative expectations do not correlate with contributions after controlling for personal normative beliefs.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Authors explicitly report replication of most findings and identify two exceptions. Later discussion confirms particular findings without overriding the results’ qualified overall verdict.

reasoning: New Spanish participants re-run the experiment reported in reference 18, comparing behavioural types and causal norm effects. Tightness-looseness studies motivate the pandemic extension but their original cross-sectional findings are not directly re-tested; the collective-risk task source is a materials source, not the target. Re-use of Wave 1 as comparison baseline does not itself make this a reproduction.
